title: U.S. House · Nevada's 3rd District
area: Southern and western Las Vegas Valley suburbs in Clark County, including Henderson and Summerlin.

context.text: Incumbent Susie Lee (D) won the Democratic primary and faces Republican nominee Marty O'Donnell in the general election. The district last elected a Republican in 2014; Lee won re-election 52.0%-48.0% in 2022 and 51.4%-48.6% in 2024, while Donald Trump defeated Kamala Harris 49.5%-48.8% in the district in 2024. As of July 2026, major election forecasters rated the race Lean Democratic.

summary.text: Susie Lee is the Democratic incumbent in Nevada's 3rd District, first elected in 2018. Born in Canton, Ohio, and educated at Carnegie Mellon University, she moved to Las Vegas in 1993 and worked as a policy consultant and in education and homelessness nonprofits before entering Congress. She sits on the House Appropriations Committee, and her official biography describes her as a member of the Problem Solvers Caucus and the New Democrats Coalition.

background.text: Born in Canton, Ohio, in 1966; her official biography says she was born into a working family of ten and her father, a military veteran, worked at a steel plant.

Earned a bachelor's degree in policy and management (1989) and a master's degree in public policy and management (1990) from Carnegie Mellon University; her official biography says she worked her way through with scholarships, loans, and part-time jobs.
After college, worked at an environmental and economic consulting firm in Massachusetts that specialized in water resource issues.
Moved to Las Vegas in 1993, where she worked as a campaign policy advisor to Las Vegas Mayor Jan Laverty Jones and founded a homeless shelter for parents and children in need.

Her official biography says she became a leader in education nonprofits in Las Vegas, founding After School All Stars and later serving as president of Communities In Schools of Nevada (board president from 2010), a program aimed at lowering high school dropout rates.
Elected to the U.S. House in 2018 and re-elected in 2020, 2022 (52.0%-48.0%), and 2024 (51.4%-48.6%).

Serves on the House Appropriations Committee (Energy and Water Development, and Defense subcommittees) and the Natural Resources Committee in 2025-2026; earlier terms included Education and the Workforce, Veterans' Affairs, and other Appropriations subcommittees.

According to her official biography, she is Battleground Leadership Representative in the Democratic Caucus, a position she created in 2022, and a member of the Problem Solvers Caucus and New Democrats Coalition.
According to her official biography, she lives in Las Vegas and has two children.

positions.summary: In a Nevada Independent interview she said Congress should not pass the SAVE America Act, calling it an attempt to disenfranchise millions of Americans and noting that many lack the proof-of-citizenship documents it would require to register.
positions.quote: an attempt by the Trump administration to disenfranchise millions of Americans,

positions.summary: In a Nevada Independent interview she said she cosponsored a bipartisan bill to extend the Affordable Care Act tax credits and noted she voted against the One Big Beautiful Bill Act over its Medicaid cuts.
positions.quote: voted against the Big Beautiful Bill that cut Medicaid in order to get tax breaks to millionaires.

positions.summary: In a Nevada Independent interview she agreed that President Trump's tariffs have harmed Nevada, citing a drop in Canadian tourism and higher home costs.

summary.text: Marty O'Donnell is the Republican nominee in Nevada's 3rd District. A composer and audio director best known for the music of the Halo video game series, he has not previously held public office; he finished fourth in the 2024 Republican primary for this seat. His campaign website says he is running on the message that "one good job should be enough."

background.text: Describes an upbringing in a middle-class family in which his father was a filmmaker and his mother a piano teacher; he studied piano and then composition at Wheaton College and later did graduate study toward a master's degree in music composition, according to a 2026 Nevada Independent interview profile.
Began his career writing music for television and radio commercials, including a Flintstones vitamins jingle.

Became known in the video game industry as composer and sound designer for the Halo series; he was audio director at the game developer Bungie for over a decade, including after Microsoft acquired the studio in 2000 and he moved to Seattle.
Collaborated with Paul McCartney on the orchestral suite Music of the Spheres for the 2014 game Destiny.
Moved to Southern Nevada in 2021; the Nevada Independent reports he has volunteered in positions at the Center for Faith and Culture, a Washington State nonprofit, without salary.
Ran in the 2024 Republican primary for Nevada's 3rd District and placed fourth with 20.4% of the vote, after spending more than $1 million of his own money.
Endorsed by Gov. Joe Lombardo and won the June 9, 2026 Republican primary; he has loaned his campaign $3 million.

positions.summary: In a Nevada Independent questionnaire he answered yes to passing the SAVE America Act.
In a Nevada Independent questionnaire he answered no to reinstating Affordable Care Act premium subsidies and yes to Medicaid work requirements.
positions.quote: Reinstating these subsidies won't fix our healthcare system that Democrats broke

positions.summary: In a Nevada Independent questionnaire he defended President Trump's tariffs as a tool of trade diplomacy and national security.
positions.quote: President Trump uses tariffs as a form of diplomacy to level the playing field on trade or to protect our national security

summary.text: Jon Kamerath is the Independent American Party candidate in Nevada's 3rd District. Ballotpedia lists earlier campaigns for the Nevada Assembly (2010) and Nevada State Senate (2014); he has not completed a Ballotpedia survey for 2026.

background.text: Ran for the Nevada Assembly in 2010, winning a June 8 primary 2,866 to 1,359 over Annie Black and then losing the November general election to John Hambrick (R), with David Lerner (D) also on the ballot.
Ran as the Independent American candidate for Nevada State Senate District 8 in 2014 and received 3.9% of the vote (1,119 votes) in a race won by Patricia Farley (R).
His 2014 campaign website said he would sponsor legislation to reduce the size of government, cut spending, and cut taxes, specifically property and sales taxes.

priorities.text: Lists affordability as an issue, including eliminating the federal gas tax and a national ban on property tax on primary homes.
priorities.quote: Jon wants to eliminate the Federal gas tax and put a national ban on property tax for people's primary home.

priorities.text: Lists defending Nevada water rights as an issue.
priorities.quote: Jon will defend water rights for the people of Nevada.

statements.quote: Jon believes in the sanctity of human life. All human life is precious, and he seeks to protect those who are least able to protect themselves.

researchNotes: Federal key votes and FEC finance totals for Lee are added separately by script. Ballotpedia's dedicated page for Marty O'Donnell was unreachable during research; his general-election qualification and party are confirmed from the statewide 2026 U.S. House elections page and the district-race coverage on Susie Lee's Ballotpedia page. No campaign website or public statements were found for O'Donnell or for Independent American Party candidate Jon Kamerath. Jon Kamerath: his campaign site (jonkamerath.org) was loaded and has brief issue statements on affordability, water and abortion; no questionnaire answers or news interviews were found, so depth stays minimal. O'Donnell's campaign site and Nevada Independent profiles were used for his biography. No public statements or biography beyond his election history were found for Independent American Party candidate Jon Kamerath. Kamerath's occupation, education, and residence could not be found in public sources.
